tools.name: Agentlinter
tools.why: A lint for prompts. It reads SECURITY.md and AGENTS.md, documents for people, and asks every absolute rule for an escape hatch; on 2026-11-18 it also said CONTRIBUTING.md, which is at the root, does not exist. This repository has no prompt it would be right about.

tools.name: TSQLLint
tools.why: A linter for SQL Server's T-SQL. The one SQL file, apps/web/db/001_accounts.sql, is PostgreSQL, and every finding asked for a SET statement PostgreSQL does not have.

patterns.why: It matches a key with "token" in its name. Here that is input_tokens, prompt_tokens, max_tokens: counts of model tokens, which is what this product prices, in 60 places outside the tests and 242 inside on 2026-11-18. Credentials are held by GitHub secret scanning and the CLI's own redaction tests.

File length. The 16 files it named are long because each is one thing kept in one place on purpose: the price catalogue, the phrase dictionaries, the message types. Lizard's patterns for a function's length and complexity stay on.

dismissed.why: The one-shot archive job takes a version, a commit and a flag at dispatch. Each reaches the script through env, never spliced into it, and is refused unless it is X.Y.Z and a 40-character sha that package.json at that commit agrees with. It publishes nothing to npm.

The connection string in the PostgreSQL step names the throwaway role and password that the same step creates in the runner's own PostgreSQL, started for that step, empty, reachable only on the runner's loopback, and gone with the runner.
`log = () => {}` is the default of an injected logger: called without one, postComment logs nothing. The tests pass their own.
`log = () => {}` is the default of an injected logger: called without one, suggestFixes logs nothing. The tests pass their own.
readFileImpl reads TRAZUM_BODY_PATH, a file the Action's own previous step wrote under the runner's temp directory, set in action.yml; nothing a pull request writes names the path.
readFileImpl reads the report path the Action's own previous step wrote, set in action.yml; nothing a pull request writes names the path.

`/^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@/gm` reads the hunk headers of a pull request's diff from GitHub: measured linear, 0.005 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.001 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("@@ -" then digits and commas). Each optional part starts with a literal, so nothing can be matched two ways.

esc() replaces &, <, >, " and ' in that order, & first, which is the whole of what HTML text and quoted attributes need; every interpolation in the report goes through it, and the CLI tests feed it hostile labels.

esc() escapes &, < and > for the SVG's text, which is the CLI's own transcript of the repository's examples. Reading it found the one attribute it wrote, aria-label, did not escape a quotation mark; that is fixed in #772 (attribute()), and the finding about replaceAll itself is wrong. attribute() adds the quotation mark to esc() for the one attribute; it is the second of the two.

SLUG, `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`: measured linear, 1.77 ms at 400,000 characters of "a-" then "!" (0.27 ms at 100,000). The hyphen separates the repetitions, so they cannot overlap. It checks the slugs this repository writes.

HR (five uses) and TABLE_DELIM (two) were measured linear: 3 to 9.6 ms at 400,000 characters on their worst inputs, 4.5 to 9 times as long for 4 times the text. They read one line of the repository's own documents when the docs site is built.
npm run done runs the command lines written in its own CRITERIA table, which are shell lines on purpose (pipes, &&); nothing from outside the repository reaches `line`.
DOC_LOADERS[slug]() runs only after Object.hasOwn(DOC_LOADERS, slug): the slug from the address can only name a loader the build wrote, never constructor or __proto__.
RELEASE_LOADERS[version]() runs only after Object.hasOwn(RELEASE_LOADERS, version): the version from the address can only name a loader the build wrote.
WHERE_ONLY[phrase]?.(body) looks up a phrase of the module's own dictionaries in a constant object of three functions (please, kindly, bitte); no text a caller sends is the key.
getMessages(locale).suggest[reason]() indexes the message catalogue by a RejectedReason, a union of this package's own codes checked by the compiler.
RANKS[name]() is reached with a KnownEncoding, the encoding tiktoken names for a model; a model it does not know is refused before this.

Object.assign(usage, ...) copies the object cacheWriteBreakdown or openAiWrites built, which holds only the named cache-write counts, each checked to be a finite non-negative number; no key of the provider's answer is copied.

Every pattern here is built from the module's own constants or a phrase of its dictionaries, escaped (phraseRegex, dropRegex, THANKS_SENTENCE, NOT_A_THANKS, the emphasis prefixes). All 353 built were measured on adversarial input: the slowest took 0.68 ms at 32,000 characters, 4 to 8 times its time at 8,000.

QUOTED is built once from six literals bounded at 400 characters to a line, and the other site copies one of the segmenter's literal patterns so lastIndex is not shared. All measured linear: the slowest, the e-mail pattern, 5.9 ms at 32,000 characters against 1.5 ms at 8,000.

Built once from the module's own constants (the contradiction axes, the example labels) or, in keyPattern, from a schema key escaped by escapeRegExp. All measured linear: the slowest 0.92 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.22 ms at 8,000. The loop that asked the key pattern of every sentence was quadratic and is fixed in #772. findRestatedFormat builds each key's pattern once, sticky, and tries it only at the place one pass over the text found the key.

Built from a CSS custom property name this script passes (`--background` and the like), its hyphens escaped: 0.025 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.007 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("--background:" then spaces, no colour).

Built from the heading pattern this script declares at line 141, `## The \d+ commands`: 0.035 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.009 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("## The 1" lines with no tail).

globToRegExp builds a pattern from a path of .codacy.yaml, every character but * and ? escaped, * as [^/]* and ** as .*: `**/test/**` measured linear, 0.036 ms at 32,000 characters of "a/" against 0.018 ms at 8,000.
Built from an indent of spaces read from TAP and a field name this script passes: 0.022 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.006 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (spaces with no "error:").
Built from a count the page printed, a number: 0.023 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.006 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("All providers" then spaces).
The script is THEME_BOOTSTRAP, a constant of this repository, run under the request's CSP nonce; nothing a visitor sends reaches it.
MOTION is keyframes this repository writes from the landing's timeline and the CLI's transcript at build time; nothing a visitor sends reaches it.
`anchor !== hash` compares the address's fragment with the release it names, in the visitor's own browser. No secret is compared.
`token !== undefined` asks whether the run was given a token at all, to decide whether to send the api-token header; it compares with undefined, not with a secret, on the maintainer's own machine.
`token === ''` asks whether the release job was given a token at all; it compares with the empty string, not with a secret, and runs in CI with nobody timing it.
`token === '\n'` compares a piece of terminal output (the match of a regular expression) with a line break. "token" here is not a credential.

The id keys one row of the visitor's own history in their browser and guards nothing. crypto.randomUUID would throw on a page served over plain http, as the Docker image serves it on 0.0.0.0:3000, because browsers offer it only in secure contexts.

`/^\[[^\]/]+\]$/` on one path segment of the route table: measured linear, 0.026 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.007 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("[" then no closing bracket).

`TOKEN`, one anchored character class, on a cookie name this code chose: measured linear, 0.031 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.008 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (token characters then a space).
`SHA`, `/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/`, bounded: measured linear, 0 ms at 32,000 characters against 0 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
`/```|~~~/`, two literals: measured linear, 0.479 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.116 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("``").
`/\s/` tested on one character at a time: measured linear, 1.409 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.322 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
`IS_ABSOLUTE`, an anchored alternation of fixed width: measured linear, 0 ms at 32,000 characters against 0 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
`/[ \t\n]/` tested on one character at a time: measured linear, 1.577 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.345 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("\n").
`ISO_DATE`, `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/`, fixed width: measured linear, 0 ms at 32,000 characters against 0 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
`/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/`, fixed width: measured linear, 0 ms at 32,000 characters against 0 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
one character class of quotation marks: measured linear, 1.273 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.339 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("\"").

the contradiction patterns of `AXES` (structure.ts:88 to 162), every one measured: measured linear, 0.919 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.224 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("redacta" and a space). The slowest of the nine is reported; each is in regex-timings.json. The second is a key's own pattern tried once, sticky, at the place the one pass found it: a lookbehind, the escaped key and a lookahead, linear in the key.
one character class of control characters: measured linear, 0.019 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.005 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
a character class of control characters and `/```|~~~/`: measured linear, 0.444 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.123 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found ("`").
`SCHEME` (line 173) on a link of the repository's own documents: measured linear, 0.031 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.008 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (scheme characters, no colon).
`UUID`, an anchored pattern of fixed width, tested on the uuid a line of .github/codacy.json writes: measured linear, 0.003 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.005 ms at 8,000.

`/^(\s*)not ok \d+ - (.*)$/` (line 219) on the test runner's own TAP output: measured linear, 0.022 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.006 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (spaces then "not ok 1 -" no space).

The markdown reader of the docs build, on the repository's own documents. Thirteen of the fifteen are linear when measured. Two are super-linear on a hostile input: the tag pattern, 1,098 ms at 2,000 characters of "<a" and spaces against 21 ms at 500, and the <source> pattern on many unclosed tags, 48 ms at 32,000 against 3 ms at 8,000. Neither ever reads text from outside the repository; a rewrite would change the groups its callers read.
one character class, on a path filter written in done.mjs's own table: measured linear, 0.018 ms at 32,000 characters against 0.005 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
`LEVER`, `/^ {2}[→·!] /`, fixed width, on the CLI's own transcript: measured linear, 0 ms at 32,000 characters against 0 ms at 8,000 on its worst input found (" ").
One character class tested on one character, a number pattern on a literal of the repository's own built code, and a TAP line pattern: all measured linear, under 1.6 ms at 32,000 characters.
Two anchored patterns of fixed shape on the bill of materials this repository writes: measured linear, under 0.03 ms at 32,000 characters.
Runs in the visitor's browser, not on a server, and every address is this app's own /api/prompts, relative, with credentials same-origin. No server is made to fetch anything.
A maintainer's script: the host is Google's, fixed, and the id is a model id from the bundled catalogue.
ask() fetches base() plus a path this script writes. base() is the constant API, https://app.codacy.com/api/v3, followed by this repository's own provider, organisation and name, all constants.
registryUrl() refuses any address whose origin is not the registry's, and the name and version are this repository's own packages, encoded.
fetchList is given LITELLM_URL, this script's own constant, run on a schedule by CI; no value from outside reaches it.
fetchPage is given the providers' pricing pages from this script's own PAGES and LIFECYCLE_PAGES constants, run on a schedule by CI.
href={DOCS_ON_GITHUB} is a constant of lib/site.ts, https://github.com/TrazumAPP/Trazum/tree/main/docs; no visitor value can make it javascript:.
href={CHANGELOG_PATH} is the constant '/changelog' of lib/site.ts.
The href is GITHUB_URL, a constant of lib/site.ts, plus a fixed path to ROADMAP.md.
Both hrefs are GITHUB_URL, a constant of lib/site.ts, plus a fixed path: pricing.ts and the price-report form.
The base64 of the job's token is masked before it is used: GitHub masks the token, not a value derived from it. The step runs without set -x, so the masking line is never echoed.
Inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): !important is what lets the visitor's wish for no motion beat every animation a component sets, whatever its specificity.

A notation preference. `:root:not([data-theme='light']):not([data-surface='site'])` and `:root:not([data-theme='light'], [data-surface='site'])` select the same element, and theme.test.mjs holds this exact selector as the rule that keeps the public site light on a dark system without JavaScript; rewriting it would move a guard to quiet a style rule.
